meetings.search_text: May 11 and 14, 2026 — Special + Annual Town Meetings May 11 and 14, 2026 — Special + Regular Town Meetings Special and Annual Town Meetings address hospital preparation, the FY27 budget and public-safety funding The May 2026 cycle combined a Special Town Meeting with the Annual Town Meeting over two nights. The Special Town Meeting approved current-year transfers, school funding, unpaid bills and $300,000 for legal and administrative work to prepare for a potential eminent-domain strategy involving the Norwood Hospital property; that vote did not authorize a taking. The Annual Town Meeting adopted the FY27 operating budget, approved public-safety override appropriations subject to a townwide ballot, acted on Community Preservation funding and considered citizen-petition articles through Article 21. Watch on NCM What mattered Norwood Hospital preparation 108–74–3 $300,000 in free cash was approved for legal and preparatory work connected with a possible eminent-domain strategy. The appropriation did not itself take the property. Public-safety override 126–40–6 on the salary measure The recurring override plan contemplated roughly $1.8 million for additional Fire and Police staffing; a related article covered one-time equipment. Town Meeting approval was followed by a townwide ballot. Operating budget 135–45–2 on the reported budget vote The budget debate focused heavily on the Town's structural deficit and the use of free cash to close the operating gap. Citizen petitions Mixed outcomes Several zoning, parking and tax proposals were postponed or referred for further study rather than enacted as drafted. Debate to remember The hospital discussion tested how far the Town should prepare to intervene in a privately owned but regionally important property. The public-safety discussion was different: speakers broadly agreed that Police and Fire needed support, while disagreeing over whether a permanent tax override was the right funding mechanism and whether the Town should have absorbed the staffing increases gradually. meetings.search_text: November 13 and 17, 2025 — Special Town Meeting November 13 and 17, 2025 — Special Town Meeting Cofsky Farm acquisition, reserve funding and a major capital plan The fall Special Town Meeting met over two nights. It approved the Cofsky Farm and adjacent-property acquisitions, moved money into reserve accounts, corrected earlier water/sewer financing, and approved a multi-part capital program including a ladder truck, ambulance, school roof, library facade work and water infrastructure.
